prompt.text: Use code 1 for a table, 2 for a bar graph, 3 for a pictogram, 4 for a line graph and 5 for a pie chart. A sensor reports the pressure every minute for 90 minutes, and engineers need to see sudden spikes. For the reason code, use 1 if 90 bars would be crowded and make the spikes hard to follow, 2 if bar graphs cannot show pressure, or 3 if bar graphs need fewer than ten readings. Enter a two-digit number: the first digit is the code of the most suitable display and the second digit is the reason code.

content.text: Decide what the engineers need to see from one minute to the next.
The readings are in time order, and engineers want to see sudden jumps. Choose the display that shows one value moving from reading to reading, then think about what 90 bars would look like.
A line graph joins the 90 readings in order, so a sudden spike stands out. Using 90 separate bars would be crowded and would make the spikes hard to follow, so the reason code is 1.
